work_experience.title: Honorary Professor and Former Director, Centre for Defence and Security Studies
work_experience.title_zh: 国防与安全研究中心荣誉教授兼前主任
work_experience.description: Joined CDSS in December 2015 as Director and Professor. Stepped down as Director in January 2022 after five years, succeeded by Dr William Hoverd. Continues as Honorary Professor. Founded the National Security Journal in 2019, New Zealand's first scholarly journal in the field. Developed the NZDF Defence Attache course and Pacific Security Dynamics training programme.

work_experience.title: Professor
work_experience.organization: Daniel K. Inouye Asia-Pacific Center for Security Studies (APCSS)
work_experience.description: Spent nearly 14 years as a professor at the US Defense Department's Asia-Pacific Center for Security Studies (APCSS) in Honolulu. Lectured and conducted research on Asia-Pacific Regional Security Architecture, Diplomacy and Confidence Building, Security Sector Development, and US, Russian, Central Asian and Oceania security issues.

work_experience.title: Lecturer, Department of Political Studies
work_experience.description: Taught in the Department of Political Studies at the University of Auckland. Served as President of the Auckland Branch of the New Zealand Institute of International Affairs from 1998-2001.

work_experience.title: Counsellor and Deputy Chief of Mission

work_experience.description: Served as Counsellor and Deputy Chief of Mission at the Soviet (later Russian) Embassy in Wellington. Made headlines in New Zealand in 1991 as the Soviet Union's acting ambassador when the USSR dissolved. Quit diplomatic career in 1994 but stayed in New Zealand.

work_experience.title: First Secretary
work_experience.organization: 苏联驻斯里兰卡大使馆

work_experience.title: Third Secretary
work_experience.description: Served as Attache and Third Secretary at the Soviet mission in Nepal.

work_experience.description: Appointed to the Board of Trustees of the Pacific Cooperation Foundation. Brings extensive expertise in international relations, security, and strategic studies to PCF's work on geopolitical significance in the Pacific and strategic competition in the region.

biography_summary: 鲁本·阿齐兹安（Rouben Azizian）是亚美尼亚裔新西兰国际关系与安全研究学者，1950年3月25日出生于苏联亚美尼亚埃里温。他毕业于莫斯科国立国际关系学院（MGIMO），1972年获硕士学位，后于1987年在苏联外交部外交学院获博士学位。阿齐兹安早年从事苏联（后为俄罗斯）外交工作，先后被派驻尼泊尔（1972-1978年，历任随员和三等秘书）、斯里兰卡（1980-1985年，历任二等和一等秘书）以及新西兰（1991-1994年，任参赞兼副馆长）。1991年苏联解体时，他作为苏联驻惠灵顿代理大使成为新西兰新闻人物。1994年他辞去外交官职务，留在新西兰并进入学术界，在奥克兰大学政治研究系任教至2001年，期间还担任新西兰国际事务研究所奥克兰分会主席（1998-2001年）。2002年至2015年，他在美国国防部位于檀香山的丹尼尔·K·税野亚太平洋安全研究中心（APCSS）担任教授近14年，专注于亚太地区安全架构、外交与信任建立、安全部门发展等研究。2015年底他回到新西兰，出任梅西大学国防与安全研究中心（CDSS）主任兼教授，任内于2019年创办了新西兰首个国家安全学术期刊《国家安全期刊》（National Security Journal）并担任总编辑。他还开发了新西兰国防军武官课程和太平洋安全动态培训项目。2022年1月卸任主任职务，继续担任荣誉教授。阿齐兹安目前还担任新西兰国际事务研究所奥克兰分会主席、太平洋合作基金会董事会成员。他是俄罗斯-亚美尼亚大学的客座教授，同时也是多个国际学术期刊的编委会成员。他的研究领域涵盖亚太安全环境与架构、外交与冲突解决、安全部门治理以及后苏联政治，发表了大量关于亚太安全议题的著作和论文，被Google Scholar引用超过265次。

Rouben Azizian is an Armenian-born New Zealand academic specialising in security studies and international relations in the Asia-Pacific. Former Soviet/Russian diplomat who transitioned to academia in NZ in 1994. Full career timeline: Soviet Foreign Service (1972-1994), University of Auckland (1994-2001), APCSS Honolulu (2002-2015), Massey University CDSS Director (2015-2022), Honorary Professor (2022-present). Key roles: NZIIA Auckland Branch Chair, National Security Journal Editor-in-Chief, PCF Board of Trustees member. Google Scholar cites: 265+. Birth date confirmed from Wikipedia and Prabook.
